description.narrative: I korthet syftar projektet att främja inkluderande, klimatsmart ekonomisk utveckling i mejerisektorn med fokus på aktörer med bristande resurser och möjligheter, särskilt kvinnor och ungdomar, längs med värdekedjan för mejeriprodukter

In brief, the aim of the project is to to enable inclusive, climate-smart economic development in the dairy sector, with an emphasis on resource-poor, opportunity-constrained stakeholders, particularly women and youth, across the dairy value chain.

The DNA-BILD's overall objective is to contribute to transform Tanzania's dairy industry by creating vibrant ecosystems of farmer-allied and environmentally sustainable enterprises that improve nutrition, enhance livelihoods, and stimulate inclusive economic growth. The theory of change sets farmer-allied enterprises (FAEs), thus small-medium enterprises with strong links to farmers, to achieve long-term growth and to sustainably scale the benefits both upstream to farmers and farmer livelihoods, and downstream to improve nutrition of consumers. The enterprises are positioned to strategically and intentionally supply and/or source from smallholder farmers in a way that strengthens their capacity, improves their productivity, and enhances their livelihoods, resiliency, and adaptation to climate change. This, in turn, will enable the production of affordable, locally produced dairy products improving the consumption of high quality nutritious and safely processed dairy. Furthermore, the project DNA-BILD will build on the learnings, expertise and working methods of the Dairy Nourishes Africa (DNA) consortium and expands the initiatives outreach to underserved populations, particularly women and youth, and enhances programming for climate mitigation and resilience.

title.narrative: Amendment to the grant agreeemnt on diary nourishes Africa building inclusive livelihoods(DNA-BILD) between the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency , Sida and Land O'lakes Venture 37

description.narrative:
- Climate smart agriculture
By January 2023, more than 32 000 multipurpose trees had been distributed and planted by 2,267 farmers in the project areas achieving 84% life of the project target of planting 38,000 multipurpose trees.
Furthermore, DNA-BILD continues to provide technical backstopping to 15 extension officers offering farmer trainings. 12,045 farmers have so far bene trained and received on-farm advisory services achieving 100% life of the project of training 12,000 farmers.
- Dairy Challenge Fund
The DNA BILD project identified and engaged 35 Farmer Allied Enterprise (FAEs) through signing an agreement for Dairy Challenge Fund support. These FAEs are input businesses (12) and small-scale dairy processing firms (25) in the Arusha and Kilimanjaro regions. Over 50% of these FAEs are owned by women/youth entrepreneurs. As part of project monitoring the score card was administered to these FAEs to assess their capacity in financial health, governance, and economic capacity dimensions. Overall, the majority of FAEs scores called for support to strengthen their businesses. Both technical and business development gaps were identified. The business gaps identified were financial management, record keeping and marketing skills. To address these gaps trainings were organised with the help of experienced business development services (BDS). As a follow up from the traninings V37 will monitor the utilization of the developed financial tracker tool to help the FAEs improve in record keeping and the overall financial management aspect. In addition, Kilimanjaro FAEs will be supported with technical assistance for value addition to fetch higher margin by selling value added products.
Example of results achieved:
An example of SME that has beneffited from DCF is Sivat, an emerging youth-owned agribusiness located in Ngaramtoni Arusha, specializes in milk processing and has benefited from the DCF support amounting to USD $8,371. Sivat contributed USD $3,850. Sivat aimed to use the challenge fund to expand his business and improve production efficiency which directly impacted the sales. Under the DCF Sivat procured 6 display fridges; 15 milk cans; a shrink sleeve packaging machine; a lactoscan and an automated bottle printing machine. The investment has generated several gains for Sivat.
1) More sales: The display fridges improved product visibility attracting more customers and reducing operational costs (i.e. transport).
2) Improved production efficiency: Using this machinery, the time used for blowing and branding the bottles improved from 6 hours to 30 minutes to brand 400 pieces
3) Improved product quality: Sivat bought a lactoscan, a device which gives real-time data on the quality of raw milk
